<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|HOLY weeke. 132|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XVI.}}</noinclude>of them vvalking, as they vvere going into the countrie. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=13}}† and they going told the rest: neither them did they beleeue.

{{verse|chapter=16|verse=14}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 24, 36. Io. 20, 19.''}}* Last {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the Ascension day.}}he appeared to those eleuen as they sate at the table: and he exprobrated their incredulity and hardnes of hart, because they did not beleeue them that had seen him risen againe. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=15}}† And he said to them, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 28, 19.''}}* Going into the vvhole vvorld preach the Gospel to al creatures. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=16}}† {{sup|‖}} He that beleeueth and is baptized, shal be saued: but he that beleeueth not, shal be condemned. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=17}}† And them that beleeue {{sup|‖}} these signes shal folow: In my name shal they cast out deuils, They shal speake vvith nevv tonges, {{verse|chapter=16|verse=18}}† Serpents shal they take avvay, And if they drinke any deadly thing, it shal not hurt them, They shal impose hands vpon the sicke: and they shal be vvhole.

{{verse|chapter=16|verse=19}}† And so our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}} after he spake vnto them, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 24, 51.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Ascension.}}vvas assumpted into heauen, and sate on the right hand of God. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=20}}† But they going forth preached euery vvhere: our Lord working vvithal, and confirming the vvord vvith signes that folovved.⊣

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XVI.}}}}

''1. Bought spices.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The vvomens deuotion toward Christs body novv dead.}}As she did bestow and consume a costly ointment vpon his body being yet aliue (c. 14, 3,) Christ him self defending and highly commending the fact against Iudas and other who accounted it to be superfluous and better to be bestowed otherwise: So not without great deuotion and merite, she and these other women seeke to anoint his body dead (though Heretikes or other simple persons may pretend such things to be better bestowed vpon the poore) and therfore, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 16, 9''.}}* she first before al other, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 28, 9''.}}* and they next, saw him after his Resurrection.

''12. In an other shape.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Christs body vnder diuers formes.}}Christ though he haue but one corporal shape, natural to his person, yet by his omnipotencie he may be in whatsoeuer forme, and appeare in the likenesse of any other man or creature, as he list. Therfore let no man thinke it strange, that he may be vnder the forme of bread in the B. Sacrament.

''16. He that beleeueth.''] Note wel, that whereas this Euangelist mentiōneth only faith and baptisme, as though to beleeue and to be baptized were ynough, S. Matthew addeth these wordes also of our Sauiour, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Not onely faith.}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 28, 20''.}}''teaching them to obserue al things whatsoeuer I haue commaunded you'', which conteineth al good workes and the whole iustice of a Christian man.

''17. These signes shal folow.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The gift of miracles.}}It is not meant, that al Christians or true beleeuers should doe miracles: but that some for the proofe of the faith of al, should haue that gift. The which is the grace or gift of the whole Church, executed by certaine for the edification and profite of the whole.<noinclude>{{rh|||THE}}</noinclude>
